meta: Is asking AI heating up the planet? One question at a time it's tiny, but added up across billions of questions a day, it's huge. Here's how to use AI wisely.

muc.title: Mark worries about power
muc.text: Mark hears that AI uses a crazy amount of electricity, and worries that every question he asks is heating up the planet.

muc.title: Tiny, one question at a time
muc.text: Bit says: based on estimates published in 2025, one text question uses about 0.3 Wh of electricity. Boiling a kettle takes about 100 Wh, a few hundred times more.

muc.title: Water for cooling
muc.text: Servers heat up and are cooled with water. One report from Google worked out that each question uses about a few drops of water.

muc.title: But it adds up to a lot
muc.text: The problem is the total. There are billions of questions every day, and making images or videos uses far more power than text. The International Energy Agency predicts data centers' electricity use could double by 2030.

muc.title: Use just what you need
muc.text: You don't need to feel guilty about asking AI. But you can use it wisely: pick a small model for small tasks, as in video 18, and write clear prompts so you don't regenerate again and again.

muc.title: One clear prompt beats five tries
muc.text: Next time you make an image or video, write a really clear prompt first, instead of hitting regenerate five times until you like it.
